proposals.observation: The GitHub workflow "Daily Blog Post" failed at 06:56 UTC on 25 June. Only one commit in the last 24 hours touches quiz state, so no one has investigated or patched the blog workflow. The content queue shows only 1 post queued and 47 published, meaning the pipeline is the main route for keeping the queue fed. If the workflow stays broken, the queue hits zero within days and organic search traffic loses its compounding drip.
proposals.proposal:
Pull the workflow run logs for "Daily Blog Post" (run created 2026-06-25T06:56:00Z) and read the first error line. The most common cause in Astro/GitHub Actions CI is either a missing secret (API key rotation) or a changed import path after a dependency bump. Fix the root cause in the workflow YAML or the script it calls, then re-run manually to confirm a green conclusion. Do not touch .github/workflows/* production triggers without a dry-run test on a branch first given that file is in the safety block list — create a feature branch, push the fix, watch the run, then merge.

Note: .github/workflows/ is in the blocked-paths list, which means Fred cannot ship this as a single-file diff. Joel must action this himself. The proposal is here because a broken publishing pipeline is the highest-leverage infrastructure problem in today's data. Steps: (1) open the failed run in GitHub Actions UI, (2) copy the first red log line, (3) fix the secret or path reference, (4) re-run on branch.

proposals.impact: capitalises on 66% open rate with stronger second-step content
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sends. Money Avoidance sits at 52.63% and Money Worship at 37.5%. Vigilance readers are the most engaged segment by a clear margin, yet all three automations appear to be running the same structural cadence. The data suggests Vigilance subscribers are actively looking for more, and right now they are probably hitting a wall where the sequence ends or goes quiet.
proposals.proposal: Add a second email to the Money Vigilance automation sequence. The current first email clearly lands for this audience. A well-targeted follow-up sent 3 days later, specific to what vigilance actually feels like in a UK earner's week (checking the account three times before a card tap, spreadsheet open in one tab and Netflix in another, knowing the numbers perfectly and still feeling behind), will push deeper engagement and is the most direct route to a discovery-call booking from warm subscribers.
proposals.new_text:
Subject: The spreadsheet is full. Nothing feels different yet.

You know your numbers.

That part is not the problem.

You can quote your monthly outgoings without checking. You have a savings rate. You probably have a spreadsheet that is, honestly, quite impressive.

And yet something sits underneath all of it that the spreadsheet cannot touch.

For a lot of people in this sequence it sounds like this: "I'm doing everything right and I still feel behind." Not behind a specific person. Just behind some version of where you thought you would be by now.

That feeling is not evidence you are failing. It is evidence that the careful, watchful approach to money you built, probably for very good reasons, has a cost that nobody warned you about.

Joel here. I spent years being financially meticulous and emotionally exhausted by it. The monitoring did not stop the anxiety. It just gave the anxiety better data to work with.

The work underneath that is not about doing more checking or less checking. It is about asking what the checking is actually for.

If you want to talk through where that sits for you right now, my discovery call is 45 minutes and costs nothing. No sales script, no close. Just an honest reckoning with where your money life actually is and whether working together makes sense.

Book a call: [DISCOVERY_CALL_LINK]

Joel
MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner

proposals.impact: converts the one session that loaded but did not start
proposals.observation: The quiz received exactly one session in the 48-hour window, that session loaded the intro screen and went no further. Start count is zero. This means the call-to-action or the intro copy itself is the drop point, not a later question. One visitor saw the intro and left without pressing start.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro screen's headline and sub-copy. The current text is not in the data feed, so the replacement below is written to the brief: it must be specific enough to make a 28-year-old who earns well and checks their account three times a day feel seen in under four seconds, and it must make the start action feel low-stakes. Generic quiz intros ("Find out your money personality!") lose this audience fast because they read them as another product promising a fix.
